executiveSummary: GM1699's official 2025 identity, generalized boundary, contained centre, 31,751 residents, 35 neighbourhoods, 21 BAG woonplaatsen, 35 BRT settlement labels, Drenthe safety-region membership and eight NWB border links are coherent. Neighbourhood population is six below the municipality total (-0.019%) and can be reconciled without rewriting rounded observations. The deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes, but the local interpretation is unsafe. The inland municipality receives 1.090096 m direct coastal inundation and 11,850 affected resident-equivalents at T+24 even though the VRD states that Drenthe has no primary sea or major-river defences and bounds its limited large-water concern around Meppel. Seven materially different active hazards reuse exactly the same leading neighbourhood order. The canonical wildfire supplies remote smoke but zero local flame despite Noordenveld's forest/peat landscape and official 2026 elevated-fire warnings; a controlled source at the official centre of Verspreide huizen Veenhuizen ranks that source only 11th of 35. The earthquake preset publishes 0.107314 g and more than 6,500 affected resident-equivalents without selecting a KNMI event, source, magnitude, site-response field or fragility, while the current SodM 2024-2025 Norg review reports no storage-related earthquakes for that gas year. UGS Norg at Langelo has a current public Seveso ramp-response plan covering condensate leakage/fire, flare fire, BLEVE and blow-out plus explicit power and winter backup dependencies, but none is represented. Pluvial, groundwater, drought, Peizerdiep/De Onlanden, WMD supply, rural access, external acute care and PI Veenhuizen continuity are likewise replaced by generic exact service and recovery curves. Dated observations, partial registers and missing topology remain context or Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open, available or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1699 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats and settlement input
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/PDOK snapshot retrieved 2026-08-31; BRT source date 2025-07-01
supports: CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1699 as Noordenveld in Drenthe and reports 31,751 residents, density 160/km2, 29.1% aged 65 or older and 4,708 one-person households. The generated centre [6.422027043143912, 53.08442370251972] is inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Thirty-five neighbourhood rows in five districts sum to 31,745 residents, six below the municipality total (-0.019%); households sum to 14,405 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 9,260. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 31,751 without changing source observations.

All 21 BAG woonplaats centres are contained. The BRT bundle supplies 35 independent settlement labels: 16 woonkernen, 17 buurtschappen and two deelkernen. BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0; generated regional source metadata reports CBS CC BY 4.0.

All rows have population, household, age, land and water fields, but home value covers 30/35, cars per household 25/35, housing/benefit fields 31/35, doctor/supermarket distance 34/35, and district heat/public charging 0/35. Missing, suppressed, not-applicable and published zero remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — NWB-Light 2026-08-01, ProRail station and scheduled-transit context consumed by the simulator
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 2026-08-01; ProRail/OVapi snapshots retrieved 2026-08-31; NWB CC0 1.0
supports: Eight logical regional links use N372, N373, N386, N858, N919 and N979 geometry toward Tynaarlo, Midden-Drenthe, Ooststellingwerf, Westerkwartier and Groningen; both N372 and N979 form separate series edges rather than additive parallel capacity.
Every link has synthetic nominal scenario capacity 150. NWB validates road identity and geometry, not emergency throughput, passability, utility transfer or restoration.
No ProRail station point is inside GM1699. Fifty-seven GTFS stop areas demonstrate scheduled bus coverage, not incident-time vehicles, road access, timetable performance or evacuation capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Programma Duurzaam Noordenveld: wateroverlast, droogte and heat adaptation
evidenceSources.edition: programme document published by 2022; local strategy horizon 2021-2031 and action agenda 2021-2025; reuse licence not stated in the document
supports: The municipality reports mapped nuisance locations from a stress test and uses retention, separated sewers and wadis to address intense rain and drought.
Norg-west is explicitly linked to water-nuisance work using separated sewerage and added water storage. The programme also treats heat in settlements and agricultural areas.
Programme targets and stated 2025 intentions do not establish current completion, operational state, drainage capacity or T+72 performance.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Dated 2026 elevated nature-fire warning
evidenceSources.edition: municipal notice published 2026-04-30 for conditions from 2026-04-29; reuse terms not stated
supports: Noordenveld documented elevated nature-fire risk after prolonged drought and rising temperature from 29 April 2026 and warned that a starting fire could develop and spread quickly.

This dated notice demonstrates local plausibility but is expired historical context unless a separate current authority status confirms otherwise; it is not a scenario-time fuel/moisture field or forecast.

Municipal advice is to leave toward a road, hardened area or built-up area, move perpendicular rather than toward the fire and report precise location to 112. This is response guidance, not a modelled evacuation route or guaranteed access state.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025
evidenceSources.edition: adopted risk profile 2025; reuse licence not stated on the PDF
supports: VRD identifies prolonged rain with saturated systems, high receiving and groundwater levels, overflowing brooks/canals and road closures, plus local cloudbursts; a 70 mm/hour event can flood streets, cellars, houses and low roads.

VRD states Drenthe has no primary defences against sea or major-river water and describes only limited large-water risk around Meppel, with days of lead time for high water. This contradicts direct coastal inundation in Noordenveld.

Nature fire, drought/heat, storm, vital-service cascade, cyber, transport of dangerous substances and induced earthquakes are separate risk families. Heavy rain can interrupt utilities away from visibly flooded locations.

Drenthe drinking water is abstracted from groundwater by WMD, Waterbedrijf Groningen and Vitens at sixteen locations. Presence of those systems does not disclose local topology, reserve or incident state.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Rampbestrijdingsplan Underground Gas Storage Norg 2025, public version
evidenceSources.edition: revised and adopted 2025; public Seveso response plan; reuse licence not stated
supports: UGS Norg is at Westerstukkenweg 2, Langelo in Noordenveld. The public plan addresses condensate leakage or pool fire, flare fire, condensate-tank BLEVE and threatened blow-out at GRIP 1-3.
Nearby housing is approximately 250-300 m from the site and a public road passes it. The scenarios can have health, off-site, administrative or environmental effects.

The site includes a 110 kV switching/transformer station. The plan says UGS Norg is an essential household-gas supplier and that diesel generators are placed in winter to enable gas production during large-scale electricity failure; this is a seasonal documented dependency, not proof of indefinite backup.

The plan identifies NAM operational expertise, Meldkamer Noord-Nederland, public reporting out of hours and scenario-specific coordination. None of those roles or resource states is represented by the generic cyber, fire or gas service curves.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Peizerdiep and De Onlanden water-system adaptation
evidenceSources.edition: project update 2025-09-08; first phase expected through 2027; page reuse licence not stated
supports: The Peizerdiep drains toward De Onlanden; current work is intended to slow discharge, retain water, reduce flood risk and preserve peat during wet winters and dry summers.
The project describes present pumping by gemaal Weehorst, future natural level rise, Oude Diep co-flow during high water and a design phase expected to finish its first implementation stage in 2027.
Project intent is not evidence that future measures are already operational, and the water ultimately being routed toward the sea does not make a Noordenveld cloudburst a direct coastal-surge event.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Assessment of the 2024-2025 annual report for gas storage Norg
evidenceSources.edition: assessment dated 2026-06-08 of gas year 2024-2025; reuse licence not stated on the page
supports: SodM reports that NAM stayed within the approved Norg gas-volume and pressure limits, found no integrity-relevant discrepancies and measured no earthquakes related to the storage during gas year 2024-2025.

Storage operators must control containment, pressure and seismic risk. A compliant past reporting period and zero related recorded events are not a zero future hazard, forecast or licence to assign a deterministic PGA field.
Public NLOG/SodM material treats seismicity, soil rise/subsidence and storage integrity as monitored but distinct mechanisms. They must not be collapsed into one Groningen-centred damage curve.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — National IMWA/DAMO water-control and wastewater public context snapshot
evidenceSources.edition: deployment snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03T01:38:15Z; CC BY-SA 4.0; explicitly partial national aggregation
supports: Only three points are assigned inside GM1699: surface-water pump Kloosterveen (manager Waterschap Drents Overijsselse Delta, reported capacity 58.8) and two Wetterskip Fryslan weirs with null capacity.

No Noorderzijlvest pump, sewer pump, sluice or wastewater-treatment point is assigned. Because contributing-water-board completeness varies, this is a coverage gap rather than evidence that those assets do not exist.
Point capacity unit, connected catchment, live state, power dependency and restoration status are not available and therefore cannot drive exact Water or Drainage percentages.

evidenceSources.title: E10 — Vragenlijst aanbod SEHs en Acute Verloskunde 2026 v1.1
supports: No registered acute-care department is inside GM1699. From the municipality reference point, Wilhelmina Ziekenhuis Assen and Martini Ziekenhuis are approximately 14.729 and 14.734 km straight-line distance, and UMCG approximately 18.373 km; all report 24/7 emergency and acute-obstetric roles.
Straight-line distance and questionnaire roles do not establish route passability, ambulance time, staffing, acceptance, occupancy, generator endurance or incident capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E11 — PI Veenhuizen, location Norgerhaven and institutional context
evidenceSources.edition: current location page accessed 2026-09-03; capacity statement has no observation timestamp; reuse licence not stated
supports: PI Veenhuizen comprises Norgerhaven, Esserheem, Groot Bankenbosch and JJI De Haven. Norgerhaven is a prison and remand centre with stated capacity 242 excluding multi-person cell use, including special-care functions.

Institutional residents, staff, visitors, security constraints and evacuation/shelter-in-place requirements are not captured by the resident-only CBS allocation or by a generic Facilities percentage. Current occupancy and emergency continuity remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: E12 — Dated Roden-area drinking-water works and pressure notice
evidenceSources.edition: notice dated 2025-03-03 for works on 2025-03-05/06; page reuse licence not stated
supports: WMD warned that one dated intervention near Roden could reduce pressure in Roden, Nieuw-Roden, Peize, Donderen, Norg and Veenhuizen and could cause brown water, demonstrating a multi-place operational dependency.
The notice is expired historical evidence of coupling, not a current outage, complete pressure zone, emergency reserve, contamination state or restoration promise.

evidenceSources.title: E13 — National electricity capacity-map municipality sample for GM1699
evidenceSources.edition: deployment sample retrieved 2026-09-02; at least quarterly capacity/projects and monthly queue cadence; described as open data but exact licence identifier not found
supports: The single Een-area sample maps to Enexis service area VVL10 Vierverlaten and reports withdrawal queue 43.5 MW/70 requests, injection queue 18.9 MW/39 requests and five projects with earliest year 2029.
One postcode sample is not complete municipality coverage, and capacity-map planning values are not outage telemetry, current load, switching, reserve, damage, crew or T+72 restoration evidence.

evidenceSources.title: E14 — Dynamic current nature-fire risk phase for Drenthe
evidenceSources.edition: dynamic page showed Drenthe Phase 1 when accessed; the page states phases may change around midnight; issue time and reuse licence not stated
supports: The current public page showed Drenthe at Phase 1 when accessed, whereas the dated E04 notice recorded an earlier elevated state.

Phase 1 means no extra fire-service measures are reported on that page; it is a changeable present status, not zero fire hazard, an ignition/perimeter observation, a spread forecast or a guaranteed T+72 state.

identity.summary: GM1699, Noordenveld, Drenthe and safety region Drenthe agree across the consumed official 2025 sources.
notes: Feature id, bundle code and bundle name all match; the safety-region assignment is unique.
Identity verification does not establish hazard, asset or service calibration.

geography.summary: The official 2025 generalized MultiPolygon and generated reference point are internally coherent.
notes: The audit context reports centre [6.422027043143912, 53.08442370251972] inside the boundary.
Administrative containment does not encode elevation, peat, forest, groundwater, Peizerdiep/De Onlanden flow or a fire/flood perimeter.

demography.summary: Municipality and neighbourhood population totals reconcile within CBS small-area rounding.
notes: Municipality population is 31,751; the 35 neighbourhoods sum to 31,745, a six-person difference (-0.019%).
Age 65+ is 29.1% and 4,708 one-person households matter for assistance demand, not automatic infrastructure restoration priority.
The largest neighbourhoods are Roden 7,320, Roden West 6,865, Peize 4,360 and Norg 3,690.

regionalDetail.summary: All 35 official neighbourhoods and supported context fields are present, but material fields are partial or wholly missing and transient/institutional populations are outside the resident allocation.
notes: Average household size is available 35/35, home value 30/35, cars per household 25/35, housing/benefit fields 31/35 and GP/supermarket distance 34/35; district heat and public charging are 0/35 available.
Veenhuizen's prison, staff, visitors and special-care demand are not resident-equivalent values. Current occupancy, criticality and evacuation needs are Unknown rather than zero.
Neutral missing-data handling is correct, but the UI must expose field coverage and must not silently impute household or operational state.

settlements.summary: Twenty-one BAG woonplaatsen and 35 BRT settlement polygons are assigned without generalized-boundary leakage.
notes: BAG places include Roden, Peize, Norg, Veenhuizen, Langelo and dispersed villages; BRT independently distinguishes 16 woonkernen, 17 buurtschappen and two deelkernen.
Settlement population metadata is descriptive and is not forced to reconcile with CBS residents.

transport.summary: Official road and transit identity is useful context, but the eight-edge municipal graph cannot establish rural route passability, destination access or emergency capacity.
notes: Eight NWB border edges reach five neighbouring municipalities; all have the same synthetic capacity 150 and are reused for every service.

No station is inside GM1699 and 57 bus stop areas provide no event-valid operation. Internal forest/peat roads, Peizerdiep crossings, UGS approach/cordon access, PI routes and hospital routing are absent.
The RIVM nearest-hospital values are straight-line context only. Assen and Groningen destination choice depends on passability, ambulance availability and acceptance at scenario time.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative risk, fire, UGS, water and care context exists, but operational roles, live resources and first-72-hour decisions are not represented.
notes: VRD documents locally relevant prolonged/local rain, nature fire, vital-service failure, cyber, hazardous transport, earthquake and UGS-specific Seveso incidents.
The simulator has no incident-valid ignition/perimeter, water-control state, NAM/VRD plan activation, road cordon, hospital acceptance, PI continuity or shelter/distribution resource ledger.
A dynamic Phase 1 page, dated Phase 2 warning or historical WMD notice is context at its own time only and cannot be projected through T+72.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute at all checkpoints, but the coastal, wildfire, earthquake and compound interpretations contain release-blocking local contradictions.
notes: The mandated gate exercised severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

Coastal-flood gives 1.090096 m at T+6, T+12 and T+24; at T+24 it reports severity 0.413957, 11,850 affected resident-equivalents and 291,171.708 deprived person-hours. At T+72 forcing is zero but 2,954 remain affected and 964,915.915 person-hours have accumulated without a selected event or dewatering case.

River-flood remains exactly zero throughout. That is reasonable only for the named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel direct screen and is not an all-clear for Peizerdiep, De Onlanden, brooks, canals, groundwater, prolonged rain or drainage failure.
Pluvial-flood gives an exact 0.167048 m depth at T+12 and T+24 without using the local stress test, rain field, terrain, sewer, groundwater, pump, receiving-water or road-threshold state.

Earthquake gives 0.107314 g at T+6 and 6,563 affected resident-equivalents, then retains more than 6,500 affected through T+24 despite zero current ground motion, without a named event or local fragility.
Canonical wildfire gives smoke 0.258291 and drought 0.705083 but zero local flame at T+12/T+24; compound remains critical at T+72 with 0.428882 m depth and 17,747 affected resident-equivalents.

numericalInvariants.summary: The focused deterministic contract passes boundedness, ledger closure, population/demand/delivery reconciliation and monotonic cumulative burden.
notes: Initial command MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1699 pnpm audit:model passed one file and two tests.

Hazard and service causal sums close; all values are finite and bounded; affected population is integral and bounded; all 35 local allocations reconcile to municipality population, demand and delivery.
Passing arithmetic verifies implementation invariants, not physical calibration or operational readiness.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One seeded neighbourhood surface overrides distinct water, heat, cyber, winter and fire mechanisms and ignores an explicit ignition.
notes: At T+24, severe-storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and canonical wildfire share the exact first eight order: Buitengebied Roden Zuid, Buitengebied Roden West, Een, Peizermade, Verspreide huizen Zuidvelde, Verspreide huizen Peize Noord, Verspreide huizen Huis ter Heide and Nieuw-Roden. Compound shares the same leaders with one adjacent swap.

A controlled wildfire source at the official centre of BU16990450 Verspreide huizen Veenhuizen [6.4142499267973045, 53.01425505399224] produces local fire 0.363886, smoke 0.586450 and 5,372 affected resident-equivalents, but the source neighbourhood ranks only 11th of 35.

The allocator samples no ignition/perimeter containment, forest/peat eligibility, fuel/moisture, wind, barriers, visitors/institutions, access, extinguishing water or suppression; the controlled source is hypothetical, not an observed fire.
Coastal depth ignores Drenthe's inland geography. Pluvial allocation ignores Norg-west, Peizerdiep, De Onlanden and current/future water-control states.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact eight-service values are driven by generic coefficients and one road graph rather than Noordenveld's water, UGS, power, telecom, care and institutional dependencies.
notes: UGS Norg's documented 110 kV dependency, winter diesel generators, NAM operating role and possible household-gas supply consequences do not drive Power or Gas.
Three assigned HWH points are explicitly partial and omit Noorderzijlvest infrastructure; the old WMD notice demonstrates multi-place pressure coupling but supplies no current topology or state.

The single Vierverlaten capacity sample is large-user planning context only. Seventy-four RDI antenna installations (32 mobile, 19 fixed-link, 22 amateur, one other mobile) are locations, not coverage, backhaul, backup or current Telecom availability.

Facilities omits external acute-care routing and PI Veenhuizen continuity. Twenty-three DUO education records identify registered use, not shelter designation, live occupancy, accessibility, supplies or backup.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical explanations reconcile, but they describe synthetic model stages and omit responsible authority, valid-time observation and physical dependency provenance.
notes: Scenario controls and derived contributions are visible and exact, but a contribution is not an observed cause.
The public sources distinguish historical measurement, dynamic present phase, planning programme, regulated scenario and synthetic model value; the UI must preserve these evidence classes.
Unknown status, missing capacity/unit/topology and out-of-coverage observation must remain neutral Unknown/NoData rather than becoming zero, safe, open or restored.

recovery72h.summary: First-72-hour degradation and recovery lack incident-specific actions, authority, prerequisites, resources and completion evidence.
notes: Compound Power, Water, Drainage, Gas, Telecom, Mobility, Facilities and Supply are numerically identical at T+48 and T+72 while hazard depth remains 0.428882 m; the model provides no blocker or action ledger for that plateau.
Coastal forcing clears at T+48 although no coastal event is physically selected; severe storm, winter, earthquake and wildfire generically return to operational by T+72 without operator milestones.

At T+0-6 an exercise needs a selected event, issue/validity window, confidence and accountable lead; wildfire needs ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, wind, evacuation/cordon and response state; water needs rain, groundwater, receiving level, controls, roads and forecasts; UGS needs the correct RBP scenario and NAM/VRD activation.

At T+6-24 the view must track rural road passability, Assen/Groningen hospital acceptance, ambulance/fire resources, PI continuity, vulnerable-household contact, utility/operator assessments and public warning. At T+24-72 it must track resupply, relief, access restoration, water-quality/pressure checks, welfare checks, controlled return and evidence-backed completion.

Pluvial at T+24 reports zero affected residents while Drainage is 0.688258, Water 0.814439 and cumulative deprivation 74,421.273 person-hours; zero thresholded affected is not proof of zero disruption or recovery.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, boundary, settlements and population reconcile.
findings.evidence: E01-E02 verify GM1699, its contained centre, 31,751 residents, 35 neighbourhoods, 21 BAG places, 35 BRT settlements, unique Drenthe safety-region assignment and eight NWB border links. Neighbourhood population differs by only six residents (-0.019%).
findings.action: Retain official identity/boundary, independent BAG/BRT roles, the transparent six-person reconciliation and field-level null semantics; do not alter rounded source observations.

findings.summary: The coastal preset creates direct metre-scale inundation in inland Noordenveld contrary to the adopted regional risk profile.
findings.evidence: The model gives 1.090096 m and 11,850 affected resident-equivalents at T+24. E05 states Drenthe has no primary sea/major-river defences and locates its limited large-water concern around Meppel; E07 describes Peizerdiep water ultimately discharged to sea, not direct storm-surge connectivity.
findings.action: Suppress GM1699 direct coastal depth/footprint under the named preset and expose it as unsupported/Unknown. Retain wind and indirect supply effects only when separately sourced. Do not turn suppression into an all-clear for local/prolonged rain, brook, groundwater or managed-water pathways.

findings.summary: Exact pluvial and drainage output omits Norg-west, groundwater, peat and Peizerdiep/De Onlanden operating mechanisms.
findings.evidence: Pluvial depth is exactly 0.167048 m at T+12/T+24. E03 documents local stress testing, Norg-west separated sewers and storage; E05 distinguishes 70 mm/hour local rain from prolonged saturation; E07 names Peizerdiep, Weehorst pumping, Oude Diep high-water co-flow, De Onlanden storage and peat-preserving level management. None drives the output.
findings.action: Ingest a versioned municipal/AHN pluvial surface and connect rain duration, groundwater/antecedent saturation, sewer/ditch flow, Peizerdiep receiving level, control state, road thresholds and dewatering. Label current metre values synthetic and suppress local precision until scenario metadata/licence are complete.

findings.summary: The canonical wildfire omits direct Noordenveld fire and a controlled Veenhuizen-area source fails containment ranking.
findings.evidence: At T+24 the canonical preset gives zero local flame but smoke 0.258291 despite E04-E05 documenting recurrent elevated risk. A hypothetical source at BU16990450's official centre gives fire 0.363886, smoke 0.586450 and 5,372 affected, yet its own neighbourhood ranks 11/35.
findings.action: Keep remote smoke as a separately named exercise. Add source-aware direct-fire modelling using authoritative combustible-area eligibility, incident ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, valid wind, barriers, rural access, visitors/institutions, extinguishing water and suppression. Assert source-neighbourhood containment for a controlled GM1699 regression.

findings.summary: Seven unrelated active hazards reuse one exact leading neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: Severe storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire at T+24 share the exact same first eight neighbourhoods, led by Buitengebied Roden Zuid and Buitengebied Roden West; compound differs only by one adjacent swap. This contradicts the distinct official water, heat, fire, UGS and access mechanisms in E03-E07.
findings.action: Replace the common hash with hazard-specific evidence surfaces. Mark every unsupported GM1699 local map Unknown and suppress ranked numeric hotspot labels until the selected event intersects a licensed versioned footprint. Preserve service-layer-invariant hazard once a valid field exists.

findings.summary: A generic Groningen-centred earthquake publishes unsupported local ground motion, affected population and recovery precision.
findings.evidence: The earthquake preset gives 0.107314 g and 6,563 affected at T+6, then more than 6,500 affected through T+24 without an event ID, revision, magnitude/depth, ground-motion/site-response field, exposed-building set or fragility. E08 reports no Norg-storage-related earthquakes in gas year 2024-2025; that observation is neither zero future hazard nor support for this synthetic PGA.
findings.action: Require a named official KNMI event or explicitly governed hypothetical Norg event, origin revision, magnitude/depth, ground-motion and local site/building/asset fragility. Treat subsidence/soil rise as a separate monitored slow process. A zero annual local-event count must never become zero hazard.

findings.summary: UGS Norg's official Seveso scenarios and critical gas/power dependencies are absent from the simulator.
findings.evidence: E06 locates UGS Norg in Langelo and defines leakage/pool fire, flare fire, BLEVE and blow-out cases, nearby housing/road exposure, a 110 kV station, winter diesel generators and possible household-gas supply consequences. Generic fire, cyber and Gas percentages select none of these cases, roles, zones or seasonal states.
findings.action: Add an authority-selected UGS Norg exercise adapter that references the public RBP scenario, valid incident state, public effect/cordon zones, NAM/VRD roles and seasonal power/backup assumptions. Keep sensitive topology withheld and clearly distinguish facility accident, supply interruption, earthquake and slow ground movement.

findings.summary: Eight border-road proxies cannot support rural response, external acute care or PI Veenhuizen continuity decisions.
findings.evidence: E02 supplies eight border edges and 57 scheduled stop areas but no internal passability or event capacity. E10 places the nearest 24/7 acute-care roles about 14.7 km straight-line away in both Assen and Groningen. E11 documents multiple PI Veenhuizen locations and stated Norgerhaven capacity 242, yet institutional demand and constrained movement are absent.
findings.action: Build a typed multimodal access graph with internal roads/crossings, event-valid NDW/authority closures, bus status, UGS cordons, fire/water passability and destination-specific hospital acceptance. Add public facility/institution context without inferring occupancy, evacuation policy, staffing or capacity.

findings.summary: Exact Water, Drainage, Power, Gas and Telecom trajectories exceed the available public topology and state evidence.
findings.evidence: E09 is partial and assigns only three fringe water assets, omitting Noorderzijlvest points. E12 is an expired WMD works notice, E13 one planning sample, and public antenna points contain no coverage/backhaul/backup. No operator-approved pipe, feeder, switching, pressure, reserve, outage, crew or restoration topology is consumed.
findings.action: Use official points/zones as non-causal context with publisher, retrieval/validity, coverage and licence. Show exact service values as synthetic scenario indices, never measured availability. Activate dependency propagation only after operator-approved topology/state; otherwise render unresolved facts Unknown.

findings.summary: First-72-hour status and recovery lack an accountable valid-time action/resource ledger and can imply safety from thresholded zeroes.
findings.evidence: All eight compound service values freeze exactly from T+48 to T+72 with 17,747 affected and 0.428882 m depth. Other presets become operational by T+72 without local milestones. Pluvial T+24 reports zero affected while Drainage is 0.688258 and cumulative deprivation 74,421.273 person-hours. E04-E07 and E10-E11 require incident-specific warning, control, cordon, access, care, institutional and restoration decisions.
findings.action: For each T+0/6/12/24/48/72 change record authority, action, target asset/area, prerequisite, resource, issued/valid times, evidence class, progress and completion. Affected population must be labelled thresholded resident-equivalent and shown beside residual hazard/service pressure. Missing or expired status remains Unknown, never automatically open or restored.

corrections.summary: Suppress the contradicted GM1699 direct coastal amplitude and retain local/prolonged-rain, brook, groundwater and managed-water pathways as unresolved rather than safe.
corrections.validation: At all six checkpoints assert GM1699 coastal floodDepthM === 0 and spatialEvidence === unsupported/Unknown; retain a separate test that zero named-major-water amplitude does not clear Peizerdiep, De Onlanden, pluvial, groundwater or drainage risk.

corrections.summary: Replace the shared GM1699 neighbourhood seed with hazard-specific, versioned evidence and a source-aware forest/peat wildfire adapter.
corrections.validation: Seven unrelated hazards must not share one full rank; a controlled BU16990450 ignition must prioritize its containing eligible area; unsupported local maps must render grey/Unknown without numeric hotspot labels.

corrections.summary: Add a Noordenveld pluvial/groundwater/drought pathway connecting official stress tests, Norg-west, Peizerdiep/De Onlanden and incident-time water-control state.
corrections.validation: Verify publisher, version, rainfall duration, depth units, licence and NoData; reproduce named stress locations and road thresholds; require groundwater/receiving/control validity before calculating Drainage or recovery.

corrections.summary: Add a public-evidence UGS Norg exercise adapter while keeping facility accident, supply interruption, seismicity and subsidence as distinct mechanisms.
corrections.validation: Select one E06 scenario and public zone; expose NAM/VRD roles, 110 kV and seasonal backup assumptions, valid time and Unknown sensitive topology; do not infer gas-service failure or earthquake from mere site presence.

corrections.summary: Require named KNMI or governed hypothetical seismic evidence before showing GM1699 PGA, damage, affected population or recovery.
corrections.validation: A missing event/ground-motion field yields unsupported/Unknown local consequence; an official zero-event interval remains an observation, not zero hazard; subsidence is displayed separately with its measurement epoch and uncertainty.

corrections.summary: Build typed rural mobility, external-care and critical-facility context for Noordenveld without inventing operation or capacity.

residualLimitations: No public event-valid forest/peat ignition, perimeter, fuel, soil moisture, wind, access, extinguishing-water or suppression dataset is causally consumed for GM1699.
The public combustible-nature layer is eligibility context only; missing geometry is Unknown and mapped vegetation is not a current ignition, fuel condition, spread forecast or evacuation zone.
No versioned municipal pluvial raster, AHN flow path, groundwater field, sewer/ditch topology, receiving level or road-passability threshold is consumed.
No live Peizerdiep, Oude Diep, De Onlanden, Weehorst or other Noorderzijlvest control state is bound to the exercise clock.
The HWH water snapshot is partial; absent Noorderzijlvest, sewer, sluice or treatment points do not prove absence or safety, and the reported pump capacity unit is unavailable.
No operator-approved WMD pipe/pressure zone, quality, reserve, emergency-power, outage or restoration topology is public in the simulator.
One Vierverlaten capacity-map sample is not municipality coverage and is not outage, switching, reserve, damage or restoration telemetry.
RDI antenna installations do not establish mobile coverage, traffic, backhaul, battery endurance, damage, availability or restoration.
UGS Norg public response evidence does not disclose or authorize reconstruction of sensitive physical/security topology; unavailable detail must remain withheld/Unknown.
The SodM zero Norg-related-earthquake observation for gas year 2024-2025 does not establish zero future seismic hazard or calibrate the simulator's PGA.
No local site-response, building fragility, critical-asset fragility or current subsidence/soil-rise surface is connected to earthquake consequences.
Eight NWB links with nominal capacity 150 are logical municipal series edges, not measured emergency throughput or independent service corridors.
No ProRail station lies inside GM1699 and 57 scheduled stop areas do not prove incident-time bus service, spare vehicles or evacuation capacity.
RIVM hospital roles and straight-line distance do not prove ambulance travel time, route state, acceptance, staffing, beds, power backup or diversion status.
PI Veenhuizen stated capacity is not live occupancy; staff, visitor, special-care, security, evacuation and continuity requirements remain Unknown.
Neighbourhood data is aggregate and partly suppressed; it cannot identify individuals, household preparedness or operational priority.
Deprived person-hours is an event-attributable matched-baseline model proxy, not observed outage experience; zero affected is a threshold outcome, not zero disruption.
Generic preparedness, service coefficients, intervention bonuses and recovery curves have no GM1699 operator/VRD calibration or resource inventory.
